correctness.rationale: The three site differences relative to vertex four form a real basis, so with row and column gauges every weighted constant-modulus isometry is realized by characters. For two columns, the resultant magnitude of the three equal vectors varies continuously from zero to 3s, so cancelling the fourth vector is possible precisely for t<=3s, i.e. t<=1/2. A square isometry forces 4w_j=1 in each row; at uniform weights the Fourier matrix works. For t<=1/4 the cyclic three-column block has off-diagonal Gram entry 1+2cos(theta)=-t/s, cancelled by the fourth row. For t>1/3 the three-column row norm forbids a triple. For 1/4<t<=1/3, completion adds an entry of squared modulus 1-3s=t in each of the top three rows. The last column and row can independently be gauged as in the proof, including at t=1/3 where the bottom-right entry is zero. Both Gram products of H then equal s^-1 I-(t/s)J. Commutation with J forces common row and column sums eta, with squared modulus (1-3t)/s<1. Each row has three distinct unit entries, no antipodal pair. Fixing a first-row entry in any column leaves a nonzero required sum, whose two unit summands are unique as an unordered pair. Each column and row is therefore a permutation of the same three symbols, giving the cyclic Latin square up to permutations. The three unit ratios of successive symbols have product one and real sum -tau; their pair sum is also -tau. Their polynomial factors as (X−1)(X²+(1+tau)X+1), which cannot have all unit roots for tau>1. This proves the forbidden region, not just sample nonexistence. The uploaded script was inspected, not executed; it checks identities and examples, not the necessity argument.

value.rationale: Four affinely independent atoms form the simplest setting with three arbitrary relative Fourier phases and permit a sharp test of whether pairwise cancellation extends to triples. The one-exception symmetry keeps that extension problem natural and exact, and the obstruction in 1/4<t<=1/3 goes beyond the elementary row-norm and polygon conditions. The conclusion is a complete capacity classification for the family, not just an example.
